2559: An authentication vulnerability was found in an OAuth framework that allowed bypassing of redirect_uri validation, enabling malicious users to potentially hijack victim accounts by stealing authorization codes. The flaw stemmed from lack of proper validation of the redirect_uri parameter to ensure it exactly matched the defined application value without allowing changes to subdirectories.
2584: A security vulnerability allowed users to see partial notifications of other users, potentially exposing sensitive information.
6488: Weak ciphers were enabled, allowing decryption of SSL traffic.
7357: The web application did not validate the Host header, allowing an attacker to send malicious requests with a spoofed Host value. This resulted in an open redirect vulnerability that could have been exploited to redirect users to malicious sites.
17105: A vulnerability allowed unauthorized users to view the usernames of other users on the website, even if the users had chosen to remain anonymous. This was possible by changing the password of one's own account and then logging in with a different account, which would display the edit page of the previous user.
29331: The username change feature on HackerOne allowed anyone to request a username change for another user without proper verification. This vulnerability allowed an attacker to change the username of a victim's account without their knowledge or consent.
